components.note: 亻 (person) — 佐 names a person who helps or assists another.
左 (zuǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 佐.

example.hanzi: 妈妈做菜的时候会加一点佐料。
example.pinyin: Māma zuò cài de shíhou huì jiā yìdiǎn zuǒliào.
example.english: When mom cooks, she adds a little seasoning.
example.fact: 佐 rarely stands alone — it mostly appears in words like 佐料 (zuǒliào, 'seasoning') and 佐证 (zuǒzhèng, 'supporting evidence').

meanings: dialectal equivalent of 什麼|什么[shen2 me5]

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 啥 is a spoken question word, produced with the mouth.
舍 (shè) gives a sound close to shà, sharing the same initial.

example.pinyin: Nǐ yào diǎn shà?
example.english: What do you want to order?
example.fact: 啥 is a casual, colloquial way to say 'what,' used especially in northern Mandarin speech instead of 什么.

meanings: to swell; to distend; to expand

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 胀 describes the body swelling.
长 (cháng) gives a rhyme close to zhàng, though the initial has shifted.

example.pinyin: Wǒ chī tài duō, dùzi hěn zhàng.
example.english: I ate too much, my stomach feels bloated.
example.fact: 胀 commonly pairs with 肚子 (dùzi, 'stomach') to describe the bloated feeling after a big meal.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 扯 describes pulling or tearing something by hand.
止 (zhǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 扯's reading chě, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Bié chě wǒ de yīfu.
example.english: Don't pull my clothes.
example.fact: 扯 is a common everyday verb for pulling or tugging, as in 扯坏 (chěhuài, 'to tear and ruin').

etymologyHint: Celebrating 喜 good fortune 礻; 壴 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 礻 (an altar) marks a connection to ritual, blessing, and good fortune.
喜 (joy) sits beside the altar — together giving 禧 its meaning 'happiness, blessing.'

example.hanzi: 新年的时候，人们常说"新禧"。
example.pinyin: Xīnnián de shíhou, rénmen cháng shuō "xīn xǐ".
example.english: During the New Year, people often say 'new happiness' as a greeting.
example.fact: 禧 rarely stands alone in daily speech — it mainly appears in formal New Year greetings like 新禧.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 辽 relates to distance traveled.
了 (le) gives a sound distantly related to 辽's reading liáo, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Liáoníng zài Zhōngguó de dōngběi.
example.english: Liaoning is in northeast China.
example.fact: 辽 today mainly survives as part of the place name 辽宁 (Liáoníng) province and the historical Liao dynasty.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 抹 describes an action done by hand, like wiping or smearing.
末 (mò) gives a sound close to mǒ, sharing the same initial and rhyme.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhuōzi mǒ gānjìng.
example.english: Please wipe the table clean.
example.fact: 抹 is a common verb for wiping or smearing, as in 抹布 (mābù, 'rag,' a related word with a different tone).

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 筒 originally named a thick piece of hollow bamboo.
同 (tóng) gives a sound close to tǒng, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè zhǐ tǒng.
example.english: This is a paper tube.
example.fact: 筒 names any hollow, cylindrical object, as in 邮筒 (yóutǒng, 'mailbox') and 笔筒 (bǐtǒng, 'pen holder').

components.note: 木 (wood) — chess and board game pieces like 棋 were traditionally carved from wood.
其 (qí) gives the sound — an exact match with 棋.

example.pinyin: Bàba xǐhuan xià qí.
example.english: Dad likes to play chess.
example.fact: 下棋 (xià qí), literally 'to lower chess pieces,' is the standard verb phrase for playing chess, Go, or similar board games.

components.note: 衤 (clothes) — 裤 names a piece of clothing, trousers.
库 (kù) gives the sound — an exact match with 裤.

example.pinyin: Tā chuānle yì tiáo xīn kùzi.
example.english: He wore a new pair of pants.
example.fact: 裤 always takes the measure word 条 (tiáo), the same one used for other long, thin objects.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 唉 is an interjection uttered aloud, a sigh from the mouth.
矣 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 唉's reading āi, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Āi, jīntiān zhēn lèi.
example.english: Ugh, today was really tiring.
example.fact: 唉 is an interjection expressing a sigh or mild regret, used in speech rather than formal writing.

components.note: 木 (wood/tree) — 朴 originally named a type of tree.
卜 (bǔ) gives a sound close to pǔ, sharing the same rhyme.

example.pinyin: Tā de chuānzhuó hěn pǔsù.
example.english: Her clothing is very simple and plain.
example.fact: 朴 commonly appears in 朴素 (pǔsù, 'plain, simple') and is also the common Korean surname Park, written with this character.

meanings: used in 吩咐[fen1 fu5] and 囑咐|嘱咐[zhu3 fu5]

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咐 describes an act of speaking, giving instructions.
付 (fù) gives the sound — an exact match with 咐.

example.pinyin: Māma fēnfù wǒ qù mǎi cài.
example.english: Mom instructed me to go buy groceries.
example.fact: 咐 never appears alone — it is always part of words like 吩咐 (fēnfù) or 嘱咐 (zhǔfù), both meaning 'to instruct.'

etymologyHint: A woman delivering 乃 a child 子

components.note: 乃 depicts a bent figure, read here as a woman's body.
子 (child) sits beneath — together picturing a woman about to deliver a child, giving 孕 its meaning 'pregnant.'

example.pinyin: Tā huáiyùn le.
example.english: She is pregnant.
example.fact: 怀孕 (huáiyùn), literally 'to carry pregnancy,' is the standard verb phrase for 'to be pregnant.'

etymologyHint: Words 言 that must not be broken 折; 折 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 折 (to break) here suggests something that must never be broken.
言 (speech) sits below — words that must not be broken, giving 誓 its meaning 'oath, vow.'

example.pinyin: Tā fāshì yào nǔlì xuéxí.
example.english: He swore to study hard.
example.fact: 发誓 (fāshì), literally 'to send out an oath,' is the standard way to say 'to swear, to vow.'

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 喉 names a part of the mouth and throat area.
侯 (hóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 喉.

example.pinyin: Wǒ hóulóng hěn tòng.
example.english: My throat hurts a lot.
example.fact: 喉 almost always appears together with 咙 to form 喉咙 (hóulóng, 'throat').

components.note: 女 (woman) — the semantic side, though the link to 'absurd, reckless' is not obvious today.
亡 (wáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 妄, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì tā de wàngxiǎng.
example.english: This is just his wishful, unrealistic thinking.
example.fact: 妄 mainly survives today in words like 妄想 (wàngxiǎng, 'wishful thinking, delusion') rather than standing alone.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拘 describes physically restraining or seizing someone.
句 (jù) gives a sound close to jū, sharing the same rhyme.

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá bǎ tā jūliú le.
example.english: The police detained him.
example.fact: 拘 commonly appears in 拘留 (jūliú, 'to detain'), a word often seen in news and legal contexts.

meanings: cable (unit of length: 100 fathoms, about 185 m)
chain (unit of length: 66 feet, about 20 m)
etymologyHint: Metal 钅 that joins 连; 连 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 钅 (metal) marks the material — links and chains are typically made of metal.
连 (to connect) sits beside it — metal pieces connected together, giving 链 its meaning 'chain.'

example.pinyin: Wǒ de zìxíngchē liàntiáo huài le.
example.english: My bicycle chain is broken.
example.fact: 链 combines with 条 to form 链条 (liàntiáo, 'chain'), the everyday word for bicycle chains and similar objects.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 驰 describes a horse running swiftly.
也 (yě) gives a sound distantly related to 驰's reading chí, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Qìchē zài lù shàng fēichí.
example.english: The car sped down the road.
example.fact: 驰 rarely stands alone; it often pairs with 飞 to form 飞驰 (fēichí, 'to speed along').

meanings: column or box (of text or other data)

components.note: 木 (wood) — railings and fences like 栏 were traditionally built of wood.
兰 (lán) gives the sound — an exact match with 栏.

example.pinyin: Qiáo shàng yǒu yí gè lángān.
example.english: There is a railing on the bridge.
example.fact: 栏 commonly forms 栏杆 (lángān, 'railing, banister').

meanings: (of flowing water or time) to pass by

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 逝 describes time or life passing by.
折 (zhé) gives a sound distantly related to 逝's reading shì, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shíjiān hěn kuài jiù shìqù le.
example.english: Time passed by quickly.
example.fact: 逝 often describes time or life passing, as in the phrase 时光飞逝 (shíguāng fēishì, 'time flies').

components.note: 穴 (hole) — 窃 originally described sneaking through a hole to steal.
切 (qiè) gives the sound — an exact match with 窃.

example.pinyin: Yǒurén tōuqiè le wǒ de qiánbāo.
example.english: Someone stole my wallet.
example.fact: 窃 pairs with 偷 to form 偷窃 (tōuqiè), a more formal word for 'to steal' used in news and legal contexts.

etymologyHint: Lush 丰 and sexy 色

components.note: 丰 (lush, abundant) suggests something rich and full.
色 (color, appearance) sits beside it — lush abundance and striking appearance together give 艳 its meaning 'gorgeous, colorful.'

example.pinyin: Zhèxiē huā hěn yànlì.
example.english: These flowers are brilliantly colorful.
example.fact: 艳 describes vivid, showy beauty, especially bright colors, as in 艳丽 (yànlì, 'gorgeous, brightly colored').

etymologyHint: The smell 自 of a dirty dog 犬

components.note: 自 originally pictured a nose, standing for smell.
犬 (dog) sits below — the strong smell of a dog, giving 臭 its meaning 'stink, smelly.'

example.pinyin: Zhège lājī hěn chòu.
example.english: This garbage smells very bad.
example.fact: 臭 is the everyday word for a bad smell, the opposite of 香 (xiāng, 'fragrant').

components.note: 纟 (thread/silk) — 纤 describes something fine and thread-like.
千 (qiān) gives a sound close to xiān, sharing the same rhyme.

example.pinyin: Tā de shǒuzhǐ hěn xiānxì.
example.english: Her fingers are slender and delicate.
example.fact: 纤 commonly appears in 纤细 (xiānxì, 'slender, fine'), describing something delicately thin.

meanings: pearl that is not quite round

components.note: 王 (jade) — 玑 names a type of pearl, related to precious stones and jade.
几 (jǐ) gives the sound — close to jī, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 玑是一种不太圆的珍珠。
example.pinyin: Jī shì yì zhǒng bú tài yuán de zhēnzhū.
example.english: Jī is a kind of pearl that isn't perfectly round.
example.fact: 玑 is a rare literary character naming an irregularly-shaped pearl, seen today mostly in old poetry or names.

meanings: classifier for trees, cabbages, plants etc

components.note: 木 (wood/tree) — 棵 is used specifically to count trees and similar plants.
果 (guǒ) gives a sound distantly related to 棵's reading kē, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ yǒu yì kē shù.
example.english: There is a tree in the garden.
example.fact: 棵 is a measure word used specifically for trees, cabbages, and similar plants.

components.note: 走 (to walk, to move) — 趁 relates to acting while an opportunity or moment lasts.
㐱 (zhěn) gives a sound close to chèn, sharing part of the rhyme though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 我们趁天还没黑赶紧回家。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen chèn tiān hái méi hēi gǎnjǐn huí jiā.
example.english: Let's hurry home while it's not dark yet.
example.fact: 趁 is commonly used to mean 'while, taking advantage of the time,' as in 趁机 (chènjī, 'to seize the opportunity').

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi mùjiang.
example.english: He is a carpenter.
example.fact: 匠 combines with a trade name to describe skilled craftsmen, such as 木匠 (mùjiang, 'carpenter') or 铁匠 (tiějiang, 'blacksmith').

components.note: 皿 (dish, vessel) — 盈 describes a container filled to overflowing.

example.pinyin: Zhège yuè gōngsī yínglì le.
example.english: The company made a profit this month.
example.fact: 盈 commonly appears in business terms like 盈利 (yínglì, 'profit') and 盈亏 (yíngkuī, 'profit and loss').

components.note: 羽 (feather) — 翁 originally referred to the neck feathers of a bird.
公 (gōng) gives a sound distantly related to 翁's reading wēng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 那位老翁坐在河边钓鱼。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi lǎowēng zuò zài hébiān diàoyú.
example.english: That old man sat by the river fishing.
example.fact: 翁 is a literary word for an elderly man, often seen in classical poetry and idioms like 渔翁 (yúwēng, 'old fisherman').

components.note: 心 (heart) — 愁 describes worry felt in the heart.
秋 (qiū) gives a sound distantly related to 愁's reading chóu, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Bié fāchóu, yíqiè dōu huì hǎo de.
example.english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
example.fact: 愁 pairs with 发 to form 发愁 (fāchóu, 'to worry, to fret').

components.note: 目 (eye) — 瞬 describes the blink of an eye, an instant.
舜 (shùn) gives the sound — an exact match with 瞬.

example.pinyin: Yí shùnjiān, tiān jiù hēi le.
example.english: In an instant, it got dark.
example.fact: 瞬 mostly appears in 瞬间 (shùnjiān, 'instant, moment') and 转瞬 (zhuǎnshùn, 'in a flash').

components.note: 女 (woman) — 婴 names a newborn, closely tied to the mother.

example.pinyin: Nàge yīng'ér zài shuìjiào.
example.english: That baby is sleeping.
example.fact: 婴 pairs with 儿 to form 婴儿 (yīng'ér, 'infant, baby').

etymologyHint: A young man 子 carrying an older man 耂

components.note: 耂 (a shortened form of 老) depicts an elderly person.
子 (child, son) supports the elder below — a son caring for an older person, giving 孝 its meaning 'filial piety.'

example.pinyin: Háizi yīnggāi xiàoshùn fùmǔ.
example.english: Children should be filial to their parents.
example.fact: 孝顺 (xiàoshùn) describes the traditional Chinese value of respecting and caring for one's parents.

meanings: used in 脖頸|脖颈[bo2 geng3]

components.note: 页 (head) — 颈 names a part of the head and neck area.

example.pinyin: Chángjǐnglù de jǐng hěn cháng.
example.english: A giraffe's neck is very long.
example.fact: 颈 is the more formal, literary word for 'neck,' appearing in 长颈鹿 (chángjǐnglù, 'giraffe,' literally 'long-neck deer').

components.note: 亻 (person) — 倘 relates to a person's hypothetical situation.
尚 (shàng) gives a sound distantly related to 倘's reading tǎng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 倘若明天下雨，我们就不去了。
example.pinyin: Tǎngruò míngtiān xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù bú qù le.
example.english: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.
example.fact: 倘 is a literary way to say 'if,' often paired with 若 as 倘若 (tǎngruò).

meanings: short name for Zhejiang 浙江[Zhe4 jiang1]

components.note: 氵 (water) — 浙 originally named a river.
折 (zhé) gives the sound — close to zhè, sharing the same initial and rhyme.

example.hanzi: 浙江是中国东部的一个省。
example.pinyin: Zhèjiāng shì Zhōngguó dōngbù de yí gè shěng.
example.english: Zhejiang is a province in eastern China.
example.fact: 浙 exists today almost entirely as the abbreviation for 浙江 (Zhèjiāng) province.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谅 describes speaking with understanding, forgiving in words.
京 (jīng) gives a sound distantly related to 谅's reading liàng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Qǐng yuánliàng wǒ de cuòwù.
example.english: Please forgive my mistake.
example.fact: 谅 pairs with 原 to form 原谅 (yuánliàng, 'to forgive'), one of the most common ways to apologize.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 蔽 describes something covered or hidden by vegetation.
敝 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 蔽.

example.pinyin: Shùyè bǎ yángguāng zhēbì le.
example.english: The leaves blocked the sunlight.
example.fact: 蔽 pairs with 遮 to form 遮蔽 (zhēbì, 'to cover, to block').

components.note: 申 relates to stretching out or extending, tied to 畅's sense of things flowing freely.
昜 (yáng) gives a sound distantly related to 畅's reading chàng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 祝你旅途愉快，一路畅通！
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ lǚtú yúkuài, yílù chàngtōng!
example.english: Wishing you a pleasant trip, smooth travels the whole way!
example.fact: 畅 pairs with 通 to form 畅通 (chàngtōng, 'unblocked, flowing freely'), often used for traffic or communication.

meanings: to bestow an honorary title after death (old)

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赠 relates to giving something of value.
曾 (zēng) gives the sound — an exact match with 赠, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì lǎoshī zèngsòng de lǐwù.
example.english: This is a gift given by the teacher.
example.fact: 赠 pairs with 送 to form 赠送 (zèngsòng, 'to present as a gift'), a more formal word than 送 alone.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 妮 names a girl or young woman.
尼 (ní) gives the sound — an exact match with 妮, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā de xiǎomíng jiào Nīnī.
example.english: Her nickname is Nīnī.
example.fact: 妮 mainly appears as a cute or affectionate syllable in girls' names and nicknames, like 妮妮.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 莎 originally named a type of sedge grass.
沙 (shā) gives the sound — an exact match with 莎.

example.hanzi: 莎士比亚是英国的作家。
example.pinyin: Shāshìbǐyà shì Yīngguó de zuòjiā.
example.english: Shakespeare is an English writer.
example.fact: 莎 today is used almost entirely for its sound, as in the transliterated name 莎士比亚 (Shāshìbǐyà, 'Shakespeare').

meanings: used in 尉遲|尉迟[Yu4 chi2]

example.pinyin: Tā shì jūnduì lǐ de shàowèi.
example.english: He is a second lieutenant in the army.
example.fact: 尉 names a military officer rank, as in 上尉 (shàngwèi, 'captain') or 中尉 (zhōngwèi, 'lieutenant').

components.note: 冫 (ice) — 冻 describes freezing or intense cold.
东 (dōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 冻, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tiānqì tài lěng, hé dōu dòngzhù le.
example.english: The weather is so cold, the river has frozen.
example.fact: 冻 pairs with 住 to form 冻住 (dòngzhù, 'to freeze solid').

components.note: 足 (foot) — 跪 describes an action done with the legs, kneeling.
危 (wēi) gives a sound distantly related to 跪's reading guì, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā guì zài dì shàng shuō xièxiè.
example.english: He knelt on the ground and said thank you.
example.fact: 跪 is the standard word for kneeling as a gesture of respect, apology, or worship.

etymologyHint: A horse 马 charging through a gate 门

components.note: 门 (gate, door) marks a boundary being crossed.
马 (horse) rushes through the gate — a horse charging in, giving 闯 its meaning 'to rush in, to dash.'

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, bié luàn chuǎng hóngdēng!
example.english: Be careful, don't run through red lights!
example.fact: 闯红灯 (chuǎng hóngdēng) is the common phrase for running a red light.

meanings: abbr. for 葡萄牙[Pu2 tao2 ya2]

components.note: 艹 (grass, plant) — 葡 relates to a climbing plant, the grapevine.
匍 (pú) gives the sound — an exact match with 葡.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī pútao.
example.english: I like eating grapes.
example.fact: 葡 never appears alone — it is always part of 葡萄 (pútao, 'grape') or 葡萄牙 (Pútáoyá, 'Portugal').

etymologyHint: One step 彳 coming behind another 夂; 幺 provides the pronunciation

components.note: 彳 depicts a step or a road, related to walking.
夂 depicts a trailing, dragging foot — one step coming behind another, giving 後 its meaning 'behind, after.'

example.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài wǒ hòumian.
example.english: He is standing behind me.
example.fact: 後 is the traditional form of 后 (hòu), still used in Taiwan and Hong Kong for 'behind, after.'

components.note: 厂 (a building) — 厨 names a room in a building, the kitchen.
豆 (dòu) gives a sound distantly related to 厨's reading chú, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Māma zài chúfáng zuò fàn.
example.english: Mom is cooking in the kitchen.
example.fact: 厨 pairs with 房 to form 厨房 (chúfáng, 'kitchen').

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — 鸭 names a type of bird, the duck.
甲 (jiǎ) gives a sound distantly related to 鸭's reading yā, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Chítáng lǐ yǒu jǐ zhī yāzi.
example.english: There are several ducks in the pond.
example.fact: 鸭 takes the measure word 只 (zhī), the same one used for many small animals.

components.note: 页 (head) — 颠 originally named the top of the head.
真 (zhēn) gives a sound distantly related to 颠's reading diān, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 车开得太快，东西都颠倒了。
example.pinyin: Chē kāi de tài kuài, dōngxi dōu diāndǎo le.
example.english: The car was driving so fast, everything got jumbled up.
example.fact: 颠 pairs with 倒 to form 颠倒 (diāndǎo, 'reversed, upside-down').

components.note: 辶 (to walk, to move) — 遮 describes moving something to cover or block.
庶 (shù) gives a sound distantly related to 遮's reading zhē, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā yòng sǎn zhē tàiyáng.
example.english: She used an umbrella to block the sun.
example.fact: 遮 is the everyday verb for blocking or shielding something, as in 遮阳 (zhēyáng, 'to shade from the sun').

etymologyHint: Fitting 宜 speech 讠; 宜 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谊 relates to words exchanged between friends.
宜 (fitting, suitable) sits beside it — speech that is fitting and warm, giving 谊 its meaning 'friendship.'

example.pinyin: Wǒmen de yǒuyì hěn shēn.
example.english: Our friendship is very deep.
example.fact: 谊 pairs with 友 to form 友谊 (yǒuyì, 'friendship').

meanings: used in place names, notably 深圳[Shen1 zhen4]
etymologyHint: A furrow cut in the earth 土 by a stream 川; 川 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 土 (earth) — the ground into which the furrow is cut.
川 (river, stream) sits beside it — a stream carving a furrow into the earth, giving 圳 its meaning 'ditch, furrow.'

example.hanzi: 深圳是中国南方的一个大城市。
example.pinyin: Shēnzhèn shì Zhōngguó nánfāng de yí gè dà chéngshì.
example.english: Shenzhen is a big city in southern China.
example.fact: 圳 exists today almost entirely as part of the place name 深圳 (Shēnzhèn).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 吁 describes a sound made with the mouth, a sigh or a call.
于 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to 吁's reading xū, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā yīzhí cháng xū duǎn tàn.
example.english: He kept sighing over and over.
example.fact: This reading (xū) appears in the set phrase 长吁短叹 (cháng xū duǎn tàn, 'to sigh again and again'); a different reading (yù) appears in 呼吁 (hūyù, 'to appeal').

meanings: used in 崑崙|昆仑[Kun1 lun2]

example.pinyin: Kūnlún Shān hěn yǒumíng.
example.english: The Kunlun Mountains are very famous.
example.fact: 仑 exists today mainly in the place name 昆仑 (Kūnlún), a famous mountain range in Chinese geography and mythology.

etymologyHint: A body 尸 decapitated 口 by a sword 辛 , representing the law

components.note: 尸 (a body) suggests a person facing judgment.
辛 (a blade, punishment) sits beside it — a body facing the blade of the law, giving 辟 its early meaning 'law, ruler.'

example.pinyin: Tā kāipì le yì tiáo xīn lù.
example.english: He opened up a new road.
example.fact: 辟 pairs with 开 to form 开辟 (kāipì, 'to open up, to establish').

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — 瘤 names a medical growth.
留 (liú) gives the sound — an exact match with 瘤.

example.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā zhǎngle yí gè liú.
example.english: The doctor said he grew a tumor.
example.fact: 瘤 is standard medical vocabulary for a lump or tumor, as in 肿瘤 (zhǒngliú, 'tumor').

components.note: 女 (woman) — 嫂 names a female relative, an older brother's wife.
叟 (sǒu) gives a sound close to sǎo, sharing the same initial.

example.pinyin: Wǒ sǎozi duì wǒ hěn hǎo.
example.english: My sister-in-law is very good to me.
example.fact: 嫂 specifically names an older brother's wife, showing how Chinese kinship terms are more specific than the English 'sister-in-law.'

components.note: 它 ('it,' originally a snake) is labeled as the semantic side here, though its everyday meaning has no obvious link to a 'steep bank' — the connection has faded over time.
阝 (a hill/mound form) is marked as the sound element here, giving a sound distantly related to 陀's reading tuó, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tuóluó zhuàn de hěn kuài.
example.english: The spinning top spins very fast.
example.fact: 陀 today mostly appears in 陀螺 (tuóluó, 'spinning top'), a classic children's toy.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 框 names a wooden frame or border.
匡 (kuāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 框.

example.pinyin: Zhè fú huà yǒu yí gè mù kuāng.
example.english: This painting has a wooden frame.
example.fact: 框 names a frame or border, as in 门框 (méng kuāng, 'door frame') and 眼镜框 (yǎnjìng kuāng, 'eyeglass frame').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谭 relates to talking, conversation.
覃 (tán) gives the sound — an exact match with 谭.

example.pinyin: Tán xiānsheng shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
example.english: Mr. Tan is my teacher.
example.fact: 谭 survives today mainly as a common Chinese surname, romanized as Tan or Tam.

example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ wànshì hēngtōng!
example.english: Wishing you smooth success in everything!
example.fact: 亨 survives today mainly in the set phrase 万事亨通 (wànshì hēngtōng, 'may all things go smoothly').

components.note: 钅 (metal) — an old sense of 钦 involved fine metalwork offered with respect.
欠 (qiàn) gives a sound close to qīn, sharing the same initial though the rhyme has shifted.

example.pinyin: Tā qīnpèi zhè wèi lǎoshī.
example.english: He admires and respects this teacher.
example.fact: 钦 pairs with 佩 to form 钦佩 (qīnpèi, 'to admire').

components.note: 用 (yòng) gives a rhyme close to yōng, with the tone and initial shifted slightly.

example.pinyin: Tā de biǎoxiàn hěn píngyōng.
example.english: His performance was very mediocre.
example.fact: 庸 pairs with 平 to form 平庸 (píngyōng, 'mediocre, ordinary').

components.note: 欠 (lack) — 歉 describes a lack or shortfall, and later, the feeling of owing an apology.
兼 (jiān) gives a sound distantly related to 歉's reading qiàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ xiàng nǐ dàoqiàn.
example.english: I'm sorry, I apologize to you.
example.fact: 歉 pairs with 道 to form 道歉 (dàoqiàn, 'to apologize').

components.note: 艹 (grass, plant) — 芝 names a type of grass and plant.
之 (zhī) gives the sound — an exact match with 芝.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī zhīma bǐng.
example.english: I like eating sesame cakes.
example.fact: 芝 mostly appears in 芝麻 (zhīma, 'sesame') and 灵芝 (língzhī, a prized medicinal mushroom).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 吼 describes a loud sound made with the mouth, a roar.
孔 (kǒng) gives a sound distantly related to 吼's reading hǒu, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shīzi dàshēng hǒujiào.
example.english: The lion roars loudly.
example.fact: 吼 pairs with 叫 to form 吼叫 (hǒujiào, 'to roar, to bellow').

example.hanzi: 杜甫是中国有名的诗人。
example.pinyin: Dù Fǔ shì Zhōngguó yǒumíng de shīrén.
example.english: Du Fu is a famous Chinese poet.
example.fact: 甫 today mostly survives in classical names like 杜甫 (Dù Fǔ), the great Tang-dynasty poet, and in rare literary phrases.

meanings: jacket with open slits in place of sleeves

components.note: 衤 (clothes) — 衫 names a piece of clothing, a shirt.
彡 (shān) gives the sound — an exact match with 衫.

example.pinyin: Tā chuānle yí jiàn bái chènshān.
example.english: He wore a white shirt.
example.fact: 衫 pairs with 衬 to form 衬衫 (chènshān, 'shirt').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 摊 describes spreading something out by hand, like a vendor's goods.
难 (nán) gives a sound distantly related to 摊's reading tān, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shìchǎng shàng yǒu hěn duō xiǎo tān.
example.english: There are many small stalls in the market.
example.fact: 摊 names a street vendor's stall, as in 摊子 (tānzi) or 小摊 (xiǎo tān).

meanings: (bound form) to entertain at a banquet
etymologyHint: A woman 女 cooking food 日 for a house 宀 banquet

components.note: 宀 (roof) marks the setting — a house or hall.
妟 (a woman 女 beneath the sun 日) suggests ease and comfort — people gathered comfortably under a roof, giving 宴 its meaning 'banquet, feast.'

example.hanzi: 他们为客人举办了一场宴会。
example.pinyin: Tāmen wèi kèrén jǔbànle yì chǎng yànhuì.
example.english: They held a banquet for the guests.
example.fact: 宴 pairs with 会 to form 宴会 (yànhuì, 'banquet, feast').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘱 describes an act of speaking, giving careful instructions.
属 (shǔ) gives a sound close to zhǔ, sharing the same rhyme.

example.pinyin: Yīshēng zhǔfù wǒ duō hē shuǐ.
example.english: The doctor told me to drink more water.
example.fact: 嘱 pairs with 咐 to form 嘱咐 (zhǔfù, 'to instruct, to advise').

etymologyHint: A person in a robe 衣 with his heart 中 marked; 中 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 衣 (robe, clothing) forms the outer shape of the character.
中 (center, middle) sits inside the robe, marking what's held close to the heart — giving 衷 its meaning 'inner feelings.'

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngxīn de gǎnxiè nǐ.
example.english: I sincerely thank you.
example.fact: 衷 pairs with 心 to form 衷心 (zhōngxīn, 'sincere, heartfelt').

components.note: 女 (woman) — 娇 describes a delicate, pampered manner.
乔 (qiáo) gives a sound close to jiāo, sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 这个孩子被宠得很娇气。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi bèi chǒng de hěn jiāoqì.
example.english: This child has been spoiled to be quite fussy and delicate.
example.fact: 娇 pairs with 气 to form 娇气 (jiāoqì, 'spoiled, fragile').

meanings: short name for Shaanxi 陝西|陕西[Shan3 xi1]
etymologyHint: A place 阝 wedged in a valley 夹

components.note: 阝 (a mound, a place) marks a location.
夹 (pinched between) sits beside it — a place wedged between mountains, giving 陕 its meaning as the name of a mountain-pass region.

example.pinyin: Shǎnxī yǒu hěn duō lìshǐ gǔjì.
example.english: Shaanxi has many historical sites.
example.fact: 陕 exists today almost entirely as part of the province name 陕西 (Shǎnxī).

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — arrows were historically used as a measuring standard, tied to 矩's meaning 'a carpenter's square, a rule.'
巨 (jù) gives the sound — an exact match with 矩, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zūnshǒu guījǔ.
example.english: We must follow the rules.
example.fact: 矩 pairs with 规 to form 规矩 (guījǔ, 'rules, established practice').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 浦 names the bank of a river.
甫 (fǔ) gives a sound close to pǔ, sharing the same rhyme.

example.pinyin: Shànghǎi de Pǔdōng hěn xiàndàihuà.
example.english: Shanghai's Pudong is very modern.
example.fact: 浦 appears in place names like 浦东 (Pǔdōng), a major district of Shanghai.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讶 describes an exclamation of surprise.
牙 (yá) gives the sound — an exact match with 讶, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息，他很惊讶。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā hěn jīngyà.
example.english: Hearing this news, he was very surprised.
example.fact: 讶 pairs with 惊 to form 惊讶 (jīngyà, 'surprised, astonished').

components.note: 耳 (ear) — 耸 originally related to alertness, ears raised and listening.
从 (cóng) gives a sound distantly related to 耸's reading sǒng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā sǒngle sǒng jiān.
example.english: He shrugged his shoulders.
example.fact: 耸肩 (sǒngjiān, 'to shrug') is a common everyday gesture phrase.

components.note: 衤 (clothes) — 裸 describes the absence of clothing, being bare.
果 (guǒ) gives a sound close to luǒ, sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 沙漠是一片裸露的土地。
example.pinyin: Shāmò shì yí piàn luǒlù de tǔdì.
example.english: The desert is a stretch of bare land.
example.fact: 裸 pairs with 露 to form 裸露 (luǒlù, 'bare, exposed').

etymologyHint: A stone 石 like amber 珀; 珀 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 珀 (amber, a gem) suggests a precious, translucent material.
石 (stone) sits below — a stone as fine as amber, giving 碧 its meaning 'green jade, bluish green.'

example.pinyin: Tiānkōng bìlán, fēicháng měilì.
example.english: The sky is azure blue, very beautiful.
example.fact: 碧 describes a vivid blue-green color, as in 碧蓝 (bìlán, 'azure') and 碧绿 (bìlǜ, 'jade green').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 摧 describes destroying something by force, by hand.
崔 (cuī) gives the sound — an exact match with 摧.

example.pinyin: Dàfēng cuīhuǐ le hěn duō fángzi.
example.english: The strong wind destroyed many houses.
example.fact: 摧 pairs with 毁 to form 摧毁 (cuīhuǐ, 'to destroy').

etymologyHint: Freshly-cut 新 wood 艹; 新 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 艹 (grass, plant) — the raw material, wood or grass cut for fuel.
新 (new, freshly cut) sits above it — freshly-cut fuel wood, giving 薪 its meaning 'firewood,' later extended to 'salary.'

example.pinyin: Tā měi gè yuè de xīnshuǐ bù gāo.
example.english: His monthly salary isn't high.
example.fact: 薪 pairs with 水 to form 薪水 (xīnshuǐ, 'salary'), from the old idea of pay covering firewood and daily necessities.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 淋 describes water dripping or drenching something.
林 (lín) gives the sound — an exact match with 淋.

example.pinyin: Tā bèi yǔ línshī le.
example.english: He got soaked by the rain.
example.fact: 淋 describes liquid pouring or dripping over something, as in 淋湿 (línshī, 'to get drenched').

components.note: 耳 (ear) — an old sense linked shame to the reddening of the ears.
止 (zhǐ) gives a sound close to chǐ, sharing the same rhyme though the initial has shifted.

example.pinyin: Shuōhuǎng shì hěn kěchǐ de xíngwéi.
example.english: Lying is a very shameful act.
example.fact: 耻 pairs with 可 to form 可耻 (kěchǐ, 'shameful').

etymologyHint: Tendons that connect 交 muscles ⺼; 交 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) marks the body — muscles held together.
交 (to cross, to connect) sits beside it — tendons connecting muscles, giving 胶 its meaning 'glue.'

example.pinyin: Wǒ yòng jiāoshuǐ bǎ zhǐ zhān qǐlái.
example.english: I used glue to stick the paper together.
example.fact: 胶 pairs with 水 to form 胶水 (jiāoshuǐ, 'glue').

components.note: 尸 (a body) — 屠 relates to slaughtering, dealing with bodies of animals.
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to 屠's reading tú, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Túfū měitiān zǎoshang shā zhū.
example.english: The butcher slaughters pigs every morning.
example.fact: 屠 pairs with 夫 to form 屠夫 (túfū, 'butcher').

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — 鹅 names a type of bird, the goose.
我 (wǒ) gives a sound distantly related to 鹅's reading é, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Hébiān yǒu jǐ zhī bái é.
example.english: There are a few white geese by the river.
example.fact: 鹅 takes the measure word 只 (zhī), the same one used for many small animals.

components.note: 饣 (food) — 饥 describes the lack of food, hunger.
几 (jǐ) gives the sound — close to jī, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhànzhēng shíqī hěn duō rén jī'è.
example.english: Many people were hungry during wartime.
example.fact: 饥 pairs with 饿 to form 饥饿 (jī'è, 'hunger, starvation').

components.note: 目 (eye) — 盼 describes looking forward to something with hopeful eyes.
分 (fēn) gives a sound distantly related to 盼's reading pàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒ pànwàngzhe jiàqī.
example.english: I am longing for the holiday.
example.fact: 盼 pairs with 望 to form 盼望 (pànwàng, 'to hope for, to long for').

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 脖 names a body part, the neck.
孛 (bèi) gives a sound close to bó, sharing the same initial.

example.pinyin: Chángjǐnglù de bózi hěn cháng.
example.english: A giraffe's neck is very long.
example.fact: 脖 pairs with 子 to form 脖子 (bózi), the everyday word for 'neck,' while 颈 is the more literary form.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — ancient people once imagined the rainbow as a giant insect or serpent arching across the sky.
工 (gōng) gives a sound close to hóng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 雨后天空出现了一道彩虹。
example.pinyin: Yǔ hòu tiānkōng chūxiànle yí dào cǎihóng.
example.english: After the rain, a rainbow appeared in the sky.
example.fact: 虹 pairs with 彩 to form 彩虹 (cǎihóng, 'rainbow').

components.note: 羽 (feathers) — 翠 originally described the bright blue-green feathers of the kingfisher.
卒 (zú) gives a sound distantly related to 翠's reading cuì, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shān shàng de shùlín yí piàn cuìlǜ.
example.english: The forest on the mountain is a stretch of emerald green.
example.fact: 翠 pairs with 绿 to form 翠绿 (cuìlǜ, 'emerald green').

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 崩 describes a mountain or structure collapsing.
朋 (péng) gives a sound close to bēng, sharing the same rhyme and a related initial.

example.pinyin: Lǎo fángzi tūrán bēngtā le.
example.english: The old house suddenly collapsed.
example.fact: 崩 pairs with 塌 to form 崩塌 (bēngtā, 'to collapse').

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 账 relates to money and financial records.
长 (zhǎng) gives a sound close to zhàng, sharing the same rhyme and initial.

example.hanzi: 我在记账，看看花了多少钱。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài jì zhàng, kànkan huāle duōshao qián.
example.english: I'm keeping accounts, checking how much money I spent.
example.fact: 账 pairs with 记 to form 记账 (jìzhàng, 'to keep accounts').

components.note: 艹 (grass, plant) — 萍 names a small floating plant, duckweed.
泙 (píng) gives the sound — an exact match with 萍.

example.pinyin: Chítáng lǐ zhǎngmǎn le fúpíng.
example.english: The pond is full of duckweed.
example.fact: 萍 pairs with 浮 to form 浮萍 (fúpíng, 'duckweed'), a plant that floats freely — hence the idiom 萍水相逢 for chance meetings.

meanings: (of a calendar event) to come along

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 逢 describes crossing paths with someone while moving about.
夆 (féng) gives the sound — an exact match with 逢.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yòu xiāngféng le.
example.english: We met by chance again.
example.fact: 逢 pairs with 相 to form 相逢 (xiāngféng, 'to meet by chance').

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赚 relates to earning money.
兼 (jiān) gives a sound distantly related to 赚's reading zhuàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā zuò shēngyì zhuànle hěn duō qián.
example.english: He made a lot of money doing business.
example.fact: 赚 is the everyday verb for 'to earn, to make a profit,' as in 赚钱 (zhuànqián, 'to earn money').

meanings: to push or move with a pole

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撑 describes propping something up with the hand.
掌 (zhǎng) is close in initial to chēng (both zh-/ch- are related retroflex sounds), though the rhyme has drifted.

example.hanzi: 他用手撑着桌子站起来。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒu chēngzhe zhuōzi zhàn qǐlái.
example.english: He propped himself up on the table with his hand and stood up.
example.fact: 撑 is the everyday verb for propping or supporting something, as in 撑伞 (chēng sǎn, 'to hold up an umbrella').

components.note: 羽 (feathers, wings) — 翔 describes a bird gliding through the air.
羊 (yáng) gives a sound close to xiáng, sharing the same rhyme.

example.pinyin: Lǎoyīng zài tiānkōng zhōng fēixiáng.
example.english: The eagle soars in the sky.
example.fact: 翔 pairs with 飞 to form 飞翔 (fēixiáng, 'to soar, to fly').

etymologyHint: Someone 亻 who lights the way 昌; 昌 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 亻 (person) — someone taking the lead.
昌 (bright, flourishing) sits beside it — a person who lights the way for others, giving 倡 its meaning 'to initiate, to advocate.'

example.hanzi: 政府倡导大家保护环境。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ chàngdǎo dàjiā bǎohù huánjìng.
example.english: The government advocates for everyone to protect the environment.
example.fact: 倡 pairs with 导 to form 倡导 (chàngdǎo, 'to advocate, to promote').

etymologyHint: A continuous thread 纟 of silk 帛

components.note: 纟 (thread) suggests something long and continuous.
帛 (silk cloth) sits beside it — an unbroken thread of silk, giving 绵 its meaning 'soft, continuous, cotton-like.'

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo bèizi hěn miánruǎn.
example.english: This blanket is very soft.
example.fact: 绵 pairs with 软 to form 绵软 (miánruǎn, 'soft, fluffy'), and appears in 连绵 (liánmián, 'continuous, unbroken') describing mountains or rain.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 猴 names an animal, the monkey.
侯 (hóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 猴.

example.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō hóuzi.
example.english: There are many monkeys in the zoo.
example.fact: 猴 is a common animal word, and one of the twelve zodiac animals in Chinese astrology.

etymologyHint: An old 古 tree 木; 古 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 木 (tree, wood) sets the scene — a plant that has dried out.
古 (old) sits beside it — an old, dried-out tree, giving 枯 its meaning 'withered, dead.'

example.pinyin: Qiūtiān, shùyè biàn de kūhuáng.
example.english: In autumn, the leaves turn dry and yellow.
example.fact: 枯 pairs with 黄 to form 枯黄 (kūhuáng, 'withered and yellow').

components.note: 巫 is traditionally read as a picture of a cross-shaped divining tool used by shamans in ritual — an image tied to its meaning 'wizard, shaman.'

example.hanzi: 古时候，人们相信巫师能预知未来。
example.pinyin: Gǔ shíhou, rénmen xiāngxìn wūshī néng yùzhī wèilái.
example.english: In ancient times, people believed shamans could foretell the future.
example.fact: 巫 pairs with 师 to form 巫师 (wūshī, 'wizard, shaman'), a figure from folklore.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 昭 relates to brightness and clarity, like sunlight.
召 (zhào) gives the sound — an exact match with 昭, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 王昭君是中国历史上有名的美女。
example.pinyin: Wáng Zhāojūn shì Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng yǒumíng de měinǚ.
example.english: Wang Zhaojun is a famous beauty in Chinese history.
example.fact: 昭 appears in the name of Wang Zhaojun (王昭君), a legendary beauty from Chinese history, and in the idiom 昭然若揭 ('obviously revealed').

meanings: (dialect) to stare blankly; to be in a daze

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 怔 describes a mental state, being startled or dazed.
正 (zhèng) gives the sound — an exact match with 怔, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息，他怔住了。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā zhèngzhù le.
example.english: Hearing the news, he froze in shock.
example.fact: 怔 pairs with 住 to form 怔住 (zhèngzhù, 'to freeze in shock or surprise').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 渊 names a deep body of water, an abyss.

example.hanzi: 这个湖非常深，像深渊一样。
example.pinyin: Zhège hú fēicháng shēn, xiàng shēnyuān yíyàng.
example.english: This lake is extremely deep, like an abyss.
example.fact: 渊 pairs with 深 to form 深渊 (shēnyuān, 'abyss, deep pool').

meanings: to gather together, pool or collect

components.note: 冫 (ice) — an old sense of 凑 involved condensing or coming together, like moisture forming.
奏 (zòu) gives a sound close to còu, sharing the same rhyme and a related initial.

example.hanzi: 我们凑钱买了一个礼物。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen còu qián mǎile yí gè lǐwù.
example.english: We pooled money together to buy a gift.
example.fact: 凑 is a common verb for gathering or pooling things together, as in 凑钱 (còuqián, 'to pool money').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 溪 names a small body of water, a mountain stream.
奚 (xī) gives the sound — an exact match with 溪.

example.pinyin: Shān lǐ yǒu yì tiáo xiǎo xī.
example.english: There is a small stream in the mountains.
example.fact: 溪 names a small, natural stream, smaller than a river (河) or creek in size.

components.note: 虫 (worm, insect) — 蠢 originally described the wriggling movement of insects.
春 (chūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 蠢, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhège zhǔyì tài chǔn le.
example.english: This idea is too stupid.
example.fact: 蠢 is a common, informal word for 'stupid, silly,' often used to describe an idea or action rather than a person's intelligence overall.

etymologyHint: To pray 礻 alone 单; 单 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 礻 (an altar) marks a connection to ritual and prayer.
单 (alone, single) sits beside it — praying alone in stillness, giving 禅 its meaning 'meditation, Zen.'

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang dǎzuò xiūchán.
example.english: He meditates every morning through sitting practice.
example.fact: 禅 names Zen Buddhism, borrowed into Chinese from the Sanskrit word 'dhyana' (meditation).

components.note: 门 (gate, door) — 阐 relates to opening something up, making it clear.
单 (dān) gives a sound distantly related to 阐's reading chǎn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 老师给我们阐述了这个问题。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī gěi wǒmen chǎnshù le zhège wèntí.
example.english: The teacher explained this problem to us in detail.
example.fact: 阐 pairs with 述 to form 阐述 (chǎnshù, 'to elaborate, to explain in detail').

components.note: 日 (sun) — 旺 describes something flourishing, as bright and vigorous as the sun.
王 (wáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 旺, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēngyì xīngwàng!
example.english: Wishing your business prosperity!
example.fact: 旺 pairs with 兴 to form 兴旺 (xīngwàng, 'prosperous, thriving').

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 寓 names a place someone lives, a residence.
禺 (yú) gives the sound — an exact match with 寓, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā zhù zài yì jiān xiǎo gōngyù lǐ.
example.english: He lives in a small apartment.
example.fact: 寓 pairs with 公 to form 公寓 (gōngyù, 'apartment').

components.note: 艹 (grass, plant) — 藤 names a climbing plant, a vine.
滕 (téng) gives the sound — an exact match with 藤.

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng pámǎn le téng.
example.english: The wall is covered with vines.
example.fact: 藤 names climbing plants such as rattan and ivy, often used to make woven furniture.

components.note: 匚 (a basket, container) — an old sense grouped bandits together like goods in a container.
非 (fēi) gives the sound — an exact match with 匪, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Shān lǐ yǐqián yǒu hěn duō tǔfěi.
example.english: There used to be many bandits in the mountains.
example.fact: 匪 pairs with 土 to form 土匪 (tǔfěi, 'bandit').

components.note: 伞 is a simplified picture of an open umbrella, its canopy and ribs visible from the top, and its handle below.

example.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, wǒ xūyào yì bǎ sǎn.
example.english: It's raining, I need an umbrella.
example.fact: 伞 takes the measure word 把 (bǎ), the same one used for objects held with a handle.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 碑 names an upright stone slab, a monument.
卑 (bēi) gives the sound — an exact match with 碑.

example.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu yí zuò jìniànbēi.
example.english: There is a monument in the park.
example.fact: 碑 pairs with 纪念 to form 纪念碑 (jìniànbēi, 'monument').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 挪 describes moving something by hand.
那 (nà) gives a sound close to nuó, sharing the same initial.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yǐzi nuókāi yìdiǎn.
example.english: Please move the chair aside a bit.
example.fact: 挪 is a common verb for shifting or moving something slightly, as in 挪开 (nuókāi, 'to move aside').

meanings: short name for Hainan 海南[Hai3 nan2]

components.note: 王 (jade) — 琼 describes a fine, precious kind of jade.
京 (jīng) gives a sound distantly related to 琼's reading qióng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 琼海是海南的一个城市。
example.pinyin: Qiónghǎi shì Hǎinán de yí gè chéngshì.
example.english: Qionghai is a city in Hainan.
example.fact: 琼 is an old poetic word for fine jade, and also the classical abbreviation for Hainan province.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 脂 names a substance in the body, fat.
旨 (zhǐ) gives the sound — an exact match with 脂, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè kuài ròu de zhīfáng tài duō le.
example.english: This piece of meat has too much fat.
example.fact: 脂 pairs with 肪 to form 脂肪 (zhīfáng, 'fat').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谎 describes false speech, a lie.
荒 (huāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 谎, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào sāhuǎng.
example.english: Please don't lie.
example.fact: 谎 pairs with 撒 to form 撒谎 (sāhuǎng, 'to lie').

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 慨 describes emotion felt in the heart, a sigh.
既 (jì) gives a sound distantly related to 慨's reading kǎi, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他很慷慨地帮助了我们。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn kāngkǎi de bāngzhùle wǒmen.
example.english: He generously helped us.
example.fact: 慨 pairs with 慷 to form 慷慨 (kāngkǎi, 'generous').

meanings: used in 菩薩|菩萨[pu2 sa4]

components.note: 艹 (grass, plant) — 菩 originally named an aromatic herb.
咅 (pǒu) gives a sound close to pú, sharing the same initial.

example.pinyin: Miào lǐ yǒu yí zuò púsà xiàng.
example.english: There is a statue of a Bodhisattva in the temple.
example.fact: 菩 never appears alone — it only occurs in Buddhist loanwords like 菩萨 (púsà, 'Bodhisattva') and 菩提 (pútí, 'bodhi').

components.note: 艹 (grass, plant) — 萄 relates to a climbing plant, the grapevine.
匋 (táo) gives the sound — an exact match with 萄.

example.pinyin: Pútao hěn tián.
example.english: Grapes are very sweet.
example.fact: 萄 never appears alone — it is always paired with 葡 to form 葡萄 (pútao, 'grape').

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 狮 names an animal, the lion.
师 (shī) gives the sound — an exact match with 狮.

example.hanzi: 动物园里有一只大狮子。
example.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu yì zhī dà shīzi.
example.english: There is a big lion in the zoo.
example.fact: 狮 pairs with 子 to form 狮子 (shīzi, 'lion').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 掘 describes digging with the hands or a tool.
屈 (qū) gives a sound distantly related to 掘's reading jué, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Gōngrén zhèngzài wājué yí gè dòng.
example.english: The workers are digging a hole.
example.fact: 掘 pairs with 挖 to form 挖掘 (wājué, 'to dig, to excavate').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 抄 describes copying something by hand.
少 (shǎo) gives a sound close to chāo, sharing the rhyme though the initial has shifted slightly.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào chāo tóngxué de zuòyè.
example.english: Please don't copy classmates' homework.
example.fact: 抄 is the everyday verb for 'to copy,' including copying text, work, or even a police raid, as in 抄家 (chāojiā).

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 岭 names a mountain ridge.
令 (lìng) gives the sound — an exact match with 岭, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò shānlǐng hěn gāo.
example.english: This mountain ridge is very tall.
example.fact: 岭 pairs with 山 to form 山岭 (shānlǐng, 'mountain ridge').

components.note: 日 (sun) — 晕 originally described a hazy ring around the sun or moon.
军 (jūn) gives a sound close to yūn, sharing the same rhyme though the initial has shifted.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān juéde yǒudiǎn yūn.
example.english: I feel a bit dizzy today.
example.fact: 晕 can also describe a halo of light, as in 光晕 (guāngyùn), when read with a different tone.

meanings: (coll.) to catch; to seize; to capture

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 逮 describes chasing and catching someone.
隶 (lì) gives a sound distantly related to 逮's reading dǎi, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 警察终于逮住了那个小偷。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhōngyú dǎizhù le nàge xiǎotōu.
example.english: The police finally caught that thief.
example.fact: 逮 has two readings — dǎi in everyday speech (as here) and dài in more formal words like 逮捕 (dàibǔ, 'to arrest').

components.note: 石 (stone) — early tools for chopping, like axes, were made of stone.
欠 (qiàn) gives a sound distantly related to 砍's reading kǎn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā yòng fǔtou kǎn shù.
example.english: He chops the tree with an axe.
example.fact: 砍 is the everyday verb for chopping or hacking with a blade, as in 砍树 (kǎn shù, 'to chop down a tree').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 掏 describes reaching in and pulling something out by hand.
匋 (táo) gives the sound — an exact match with 掏, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā cóng kǒudài lǐ tāochū shǒujī.
example.english: He took his phone out of his pocket.
example.fact: 掏 pairs with 出 to form 掏出 (tāochū, 'to take out, to pull out').

components.note: 犭 (animal) — an old, now unfamiliar way of naming a northern tribe, treated the same way animal names were classified.
火 (huǒ) gives a sound distantly related to 狄's reading dí, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 狄仁杰是唐朝有名的官员。
example.pinyin: Dí Rénjié shì Tángcháo yǒumíng de guānyuán.
example.english: Di Renjie was a famous official of the Tang dynasty.
example.fact: 狄 survives today mainly as a surname and in the name of Judge Dee (狄仁杰), a famous historical detective figure.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 晰 describes something as clear and bright as sunlight.
析 (xī) gives the sound — an exact match with 晰.

example.hanzi: 请把问题说得清晰一点。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ wèntí shuō de qīngxī yìdiǎn.
example.english: Please explain the problem more clearly.
example.fact: 晰 pairs with 清 to form 清晰 (qīngxī, 'clear, distinct').

etymologyHint: An empty 干 fishing net ⺳; 干 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: ⺳ (a net) suggests something meant to catch things.
干 (dry, empty) sits inside it — an empty fishing net, giving 罕 its meaning 'rare, scarce.'

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng niǎo fēicháng hǎnjiàn.
example.english: This kind of bird is very rare.
example.fact: 罕 pairs with 见 to form 罕见 (hǎnjiàn, 'rare, seldom seen').

meanings: to draw (a cart or a bow)

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 挽 describes pulling or drawing something back with the hand.
免 (miǎn) gives a sound distantly related to 挽's reading wǎn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他挽着妈妈的手臂散步。
example.pinyin: Tā wǎnzhe māma de shǒubì sànbù.
example.english: He walked arm-in-arm with his mom.
example.fact: 挽 describes linking arms or pulling something back, as in 挽救 (wǎnjiù, 'to save, to rescue').

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 脾 names a body organ, the spleen.
卑 (bēi) gives a sound close to pí, sharing a related initial though the rhyme has shifted.

example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le tā de pízàng.
example.english: The doctor examined his spleen.
example.fact: 脾 pairs with 气 to form 脾气 (píqi, 'temper'), since old Chinese medicine linked the spleen to one's mood.

components.note: 舟 is a simplified picture of a boat seen from above, with its hull and cross-planks still visible in the character's shape.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zuòzhe xiǎozhōu guò hé.
example.english: We crossed the river in a small boat.
example.fact: 舟 is the literary word for 'boat'; the everyday word is 船 (chuán).

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — 痴 was historically viewed as an illness of the mind.
知 (zhī) gives a sound close to chī, sharing the same rhyme and a related initial.

example.pinyin: Tā duì yīnyuè shífēn chīmí.
example.english: He is utterly obsessed with music.
example.fact: 痴 pairs with 迷 to form 痴迷 (chīmí, 'infatuated, obsessed').

example.pinyin: Cài xiānsheng shì wǒ de línjū.
example.english: Mr. Cai is my neighbor.
example.fact: 蔡 survives today almost entirely as a common Chinese surname.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — 剪 names a cutting tool, scissors.
前 (qián) is close in initial to jiǎn (q-/j- are a related palatal family), though the rhyme has drifted.

example.pinyin: Māma yòng jiǎndāo jiǎn zhǐ.
example.english: Mom uses scissors to cut paper.
example.fact: 剪 pairs with 刀 to form 剪刀 (jiǎndāo, 'scissors').

etymologyHint: A vertebra 人 protruding from the flesh ⺼

components.note: 人 here pictures a row of vertebrae stacked in a line.
⺼ (flesh) sits below it — vertebrae running through the flesh, giving 脊 its meaning 'spine, backbone.'

example.pinyin: Tā de jǐbèi hěn zhí.
example.english: His back is very straight.
example.fact: 脊 pairs with 背 to form 脊背 (jǐbèi, 'the back'), or 脊椎 (jǐzhuī, 'spine, vertebrae').

etymologyHint: A bow aimed to the left

components.note: 弓 is a simplified picture of a bow, its curve and string still visible in the character's shape.

example.pinyin: Tā lāgōng shèjiàn.
example.english: He drew the bow and shot an arrow.
example.fact: 弓 is also KangXi radical 57, used in characters related to bows, arching, and tension, like 张 (zhāng, 'to stretch').

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 懒 describes an unmotivated, lazy state of mind.
赖 (lài) is close in initial to lǎn (both start with l-), though the rhyme has shifted.

example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān hěn lǎn, bù xiǎng qǐchuáng.
example.english: He's very lazy today, doesn't want to get up.
example.fact: standard, everyday adjective for 'lazy.'

etymologyHint: A hand 又 grasping an object 丶

components.note: 又 (a hand) forms the frame of the character.
丶 (a small object) sits held within the hand — a hand grasping an object, giving 叉 its meaning 'fork, prong.'

example.pinyin: Chī niúpái yào yòng chāzi.
example.english: You need a fork to eat steak.
example.fact: 叉 pairs with 子 to form 叉子 (chāzi, 'fork'), the everyday utensil word.

etymologyHint: To take another 另 by force 扌

components.note: 扌 (hand) marks the action, taking something by force.
另 (another, separate) sits beside it — taking another person away, giving 拐 its meaning 'to kidnap,' and later 'to turn.'

example.pinyin: Wǎng qián zǒu, ránhòu xiàng zuǒ guǎi.
example.english: Go forward, then turn left.
example.fact: 拐 is the everyday word for 'to turn' when giving directions, as in 拐弯 (guǎiwān, 'to turn a corner').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 喃 describes a sound made with the mouth, mumbling.
南 (nán) gives the sound — an exact match with 喃.

example.pinyin: Tā nánnán zìyǔ.
example.english: He mumbled to himself.
example.fact: 喃喃自语 (nánnán zìyǔ) is a set phrase meaning 'to mutter to oneself.'

components.note: 亻 (person) — 僚 names a person, a fellow official or colleague.
尞 (liáo) gives the sound — an exact match with 僚.

example.pinyin: Tā hé tóngliáo yìqǐ kāihuì.
example.english: He had a meeting together with his colleagues.
example.fact: 僚 pairs with 同 to form 同僚 (tóngliáo, 'colleague'), especially among officials or coworkers.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 捐 describes giving something with one's hands, donating.
肙 (juān) gives the sound — an exact match with 捐.

example.pinyin: Tā juānle hěn duō qián gěi xuéxiào.
example.english: He donated a lot of money to the school.
example.fact: standard, everyday verb for 'to donate.'

example.pinyin: Zǐmèi liǎ gǎnqíng hěn hǎo.
example.english: The two sisters have a close bond.
example.fact: 姊 is a more literary word for 'older sister' than the everyday 姐; 姊妹 (zǐmèi) means 'sisters' in general.

etymologyHint: A flea 蚤 biting a horse 马; 蚤 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 马 (horse) sets the scene — an animal being pestered.
蚤 (flea) sits beside it — a flea biting and irritating a horse, giving 骚 its meaning 'to disturb, to harass.'

example.hanzi: 邻居家的狗总是骚扰我们。
example.pinyin: Línjū jiā de gǒu zǒngshì sāorǎo wǒmen.
example.english: The neighbor's dog always disturbs us.
example.fact: 骚 pairs with 扰 to form 骚扰 (sāorǎo, 'to harass, to disturb').

meanings: to make a rubbing (e.g. of an inscription)

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拓 describes an action done by hand, pressing paper against an inscription.
石 (shí) gives a sound distantly related to 拓's reading tà, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 博物馆里展出了古代碑文的拓片。
example.pinyin: Bówùguǎn lǐ zhǎnchūle gǔdài bēiwén de tàpiàn.
example.english: The museum displayed rubbings of ancient stone inscriptions.
example.fact: 拓 has two readings: tà (used in 拓片, 'a rubbing') and tuò (used in 开拓, 'to expand'); this card matches the 'rubbing' reading.

components.note: 不 (not) sits above — a negation.
正 (straight, correct) sits below — not straight, giving 歪 its meaning 'askew, crooked.'

example.pinyin: Zhè fú huà guà wāi le.
example.english: This painting is hung crookedly.
example.fact: standard, everyday adjective for 'askew, crooked.'

components.note: 米 (grain, rice) — 粘 describes the sticky quality of cooked rice or glutinous grains.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 粘, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhège jiāoshuǐ hěn zhān.
example.english: This glue is very sticky.
example.fact: standard, everyday adjective for 'sticky, viscous.'

meanings: handle or shaft (of an axe etc)
(of a flower, leaf or fruit) stem

components.note: 木 (wood) — handles like 柄 were traditionally made of wood.
丙 (bǐng) gives the sound — an exact match with 柄.

example.pinyin: Zhè bǎ sǎn de bǐng duàn le.
example.english: This umbrella's handle broke.
example.fact: 标 names the handle or shaft of a tool, as in 刀柄 (dāobǐng, 'knife handle').

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坑 names a hole dug in the ground.
亢 (kàng) is close in initial to kēng (both start with k-), though the rhyme has shifted.

example.hanzi: 路上有一个大坑，小心点。
example.pinyin: Lù shàng yǒu yí gè dà kēng, xiǎoxīn diǎn.
example.english: There's a big pit in the road, be careful.
example.fact: standard, everyday word for 'pit, hole.'

etymologyHint: A large 百 city 阝, representing an unfamiliar place

components.note: 阝 (mound, place) marks a location.
百 (hundred, many) sits beside it — a large, unfamiliar place, giving 陌 its meaning as a raised path between fields, and later, its role in 陌生 ('unfamiliar').

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè mòshēngrén.
example.english: He is a stranger.
example.fact: 陌 pairs with 生 to form 陌生 (mòshēng, 'unfamiliar, strange'), the everyday word for describing someone you don't know.

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — 窄 describes a tight, confined space.
乍 (zhà) is close in initial to zhǎi (both start with zh-), though the rhyme has shifted.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù hěn zhǎi.
example.english: This road is very narrow.
example.fact: standard, everyday adjective for 'narrow.'

meanings: abbr. for Hunan 湖南 province in south central China
abbr. for Xiangjiang river in Hunan province

components.note: 氵 (water) — 湘 names a river, the Xiang River in Hunan.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 湘.

example.pinyin: Xiāngcài hěn là.
example.english: Hunanese food is very spicy.
example.fact: 湘 is the classical abbreviation for 湖南 (Húnán) province, seen in words like 湘菜 (Xiāngcài, 'Hunan cuisine').

etymologyHint: Cracks in oracle bones used in fortune-telling

components.note: 兆 is traditionally read as a picture of the cracks that appear in a heated tortoise shell or bone, used by ancient diviners to predict the future — the source of its meaning 'omen.'

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè hǎo zhàotou.
example.english: This is a good sign.
example.fact: 兆 pairs with 头 to form 兆头 (zhàotou, 'omen, sign'), and also means a very large number ('million' or 'trillion,' depending on the region).

etymologyHint: A mountain 山 precipice 厓; 厓 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 山 (mountain) sets the scene — a rocky, elevated place.
厓 (a cliffside) sits below it — the edge of a mountain, giving 崖 its meaning 'cliff, precipice.'

example.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài xuányá biān shàng.
example.english: He stood at the edge of the cliff.
example.fact: 崖 pairs with 悬 to form 悬崖 (xuányá, 'cliff, precipice').

etymologyHint: A proud 乔 horse 马; 乔 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 马 (horse) sets the scene — a spirited, high-stepping animal.
乔 (tall, lofty) sits beside it — a horse holding its head high, giving 骄 its meaning 'proud, arrogant.'

example.pinyin: Tā yǒudiǎn jiāo'ào.
example.english: He is a bit arrogant.
example.fact: 骄 pairs with 傲 to form 骄傲 (jiāo'ào, 'proud, arrogant' — can be positive 'proud of' or negative 'conceited').

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刹 relates to cutting off, stopping.
杀 (shā) gives the sound — an exact match with 刹.

example.pinyin: Sījī měng de shāchē.
example.english: The driver slammed on the brakes.
example.fact: 刹 pairs with 车 to form 刹车 (shāchē, 'to brake'); a different reading (chà) names a Buddhist temple, as in 古刹 (gǔchà, 'ancient temple').

components.note: 革 (leather) — whips like 鞭 were traditionally made of leather.
便 (biàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 鞭, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 过年的时候，人们放鞭炮。
example.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou, rénmen fàng biānpào.
example.english: During New Year, people set off firecrackers.
example.fact: 鞭 pairs with 炮 to form 鞭炮 (biānpào, 'firecrackers'), named for their sharp cracking sound, like the snap of a whip.

meanings: variant of 邙, Mt Mang at Luoyang in Henan

components.note: 艹 (grass, plant) — 芒 names the pointed tip of a grass or grain.
亡 (wáng) gives a sound close to máng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial has shifted.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī mángguǒ.
example.english: I like eating mangoes.
example.fact: 芒 today mostly appears in 芒果 (mángguǒ, 'mango'), a fruit name borrowed for its sound.

etymologyHint: Bamboo-like ⺮ tendons in the chest 肋

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) suggests something fibrous and stringy, like bamboo strands.
肋 (ribs) sits below it — bamboo-like strands running through the body, giving 筋 its meaning 'muscle, tendon.'

example.hanzi: 他运动后腿很酸，好像抽筋了。
example.pinyin: Tā yùndòng hòu tuǐ hěn suān, hǎoxiàng chōujīn le.
example.english: After exercising his legs were sore, as if he got a cramp.
example.fact: 筋 pairs with 抽 to form 抽筋 (chōujīn, 'to cramp').

components.note: 耳 (ear) — an old sense of 聘 involved listening carefully before hiring or betrothing someone.
甹 (pīng) is close in initial to pìn (both start with p-), though the rhyme has shifted.

example.hanzi: 这家公司在招聘新员工。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zài zhāopìn xīn yuángōng.
example.english: This company is recruiting new employees.
example.fact: 聘 pairs with 招 to form 招聘 (zhāopìn, 'to recruit, to hire').

etymologyHint: A metal 钅 hook 勾; 勾 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 钅 (metal) marks the material — hooks are typically made of metal.
勾 (a hook shape) sits beside it — a curved metal tool, giving 钩 its meaning 'hook.'

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng guàzhe yí gè gōuzi.
example.english: There's a hook hanging on the wall.
example.fact: 钩 pairs with 子 to form 钩子 (gōuzi, 'hook').

components.note: 木 (wood) — 棍 names an object made of wood, a stick.
昆 (kūn) gives a sound close to gùn, sharing the same rhyme and a related initial.

example.pinyin: Tā ná zhe yì gēn mù gùn.
example.english: He is holding a wooden stick.
example.fact: 标 takes the measure word 根 (gēn), the one used for long, thin objects like sticks.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嚷 describes a loud sound made with the mouth, shouting.
襄 (xiāng) gives a sound distantly related to 嚷's reading rǎng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Bié rǎng le, dàjiā dōu zài xiūxi.
example.english: Stop shouting, everyone is resting.
example.fact: standard, everyday verb for 'to shout, to yell.'

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 腺 names a part of the body, a gland.
泉 (quán) gives a sound distantly related to 腺's reading xiàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā de jiǎzhuàngxiàn yǒu wèntí.
example.english: He has a problem with his thyroid gland.
example.fact: 腺 is a modern scientific character, appearing in medical terms like 甲状腺 (jiǎzhuàngxiàn, 'thyroid gland') and 汗腺 (hànxiàn, 'sweat gland').

components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弦 originally named a bowstring.
玄 (xuán) gives a sound close to xián, sharing the same initial though the rhyme has shifted.

example.pinyin: Zhè bǎ jítā yǒu liù gēn xián.
example.english: This guitar has six strings.
example.fact: 弦 names the string of a musical instrument or bow, and also 'hypotenuse' in geometry.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 焰 names part of a fire, the flame.
臽 (xiàn) gives a sound close to yàn, sharing the same rhyme though the initial has shifted.

example.pinyin: Huǒyàn mànmàn xīmiè le.
example.english: The flame slowly went out.
example.fact: 焰 pairs with 火 to form 火焰 (huǒyàn, 'flame').

etymologyHint: A woman 女 wearing a beard 而 for disguise

components.note: 而 (a beard) suggests a mask or disguise worn over the face.
女 (woman) sits below it — a woman wearing a disguise as part of a performance, giving 耍 its meaning 'to play, to frolic.'

example.pinyin: Háizimen zài gōngyuán lǐ wánshuǎ.
example.english: The children are playing in the park.
example.fact: 耍 pairs with 玩 to form 玩耍 (wánshuǎ, 'to play'), the common word for children playing.
